critical_code_review_comments: Workflows.jsx openEdit() rehydrates conditions/actions from server which do not carry `_key` (server never persists it). If a user re-opens an existing workflow to edit and reorders rows, the fallback `key={c._key || `cond-${i}`}` degrades to index keys again. Consider assigning fresh client `_key` on openEdit as well: setForm({... conditions: (wf.conditions||[]).map(c=>({...c,_key:c._key||`c${Math.random()}`})) ...}).

CopilotDrawer send() uses Date.now() for both user & ai keys — if a user hits Enter twice within the same millisecond (unlikely but possible from paste-into-textarea + Enter), userKey collision could occur. Consider `crypto.randomUUID()` or a monotonic counter. Same for Workflows addCond/addAction — Date.now() could collide on rapid clicks.

Settings.jsx pipeline stage keys now use s.id which is only generated on client (Math.random slice) for new stages; server-persisted stages must also carry `id`. Verify server returns id per stage — from data flow it appears seeded stages already have ids, but defensive: `key={s.id || `stage-${i}-${s.label}`}` would survive legacy rows without id.
Carry-over from iter4 backlog: server.py at 1800+ lines still merits router split; fire_workflows still runs inline in request path.
